creation of the three in a row

d4 – e4 – f4

on the 4th matrix row.  With

* d4 = O , e4 = O

a play in column f puts

f4 = O

so that row 4 now contains O O O on d-e-f.  The two winning
completions of the four are

c4  =  c4 – d4 – e4 – f4
g4  =  d4 – e4 – f4 – g4

and both c4 and g4 are playable in one move, column c being next

two moves.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The board is rows 1 top to 6 bottom, a–g left to right. Legal drops in the matrix notation are a4, b5, c4, d3, e3, f4, g4. No 1-ply O win exists.

Key material:
* Row 4 from the top: d4 O e4 O. c4 and f4 are the two squares that make a horizontal three on that rank.
* Latent \ diagonal c6 O – d5 O – e4 O – f3 . f3 becomes reachable only after f4 is occupied.

f4:
After O f4 row4 is d4 O e4 O f4 O. Immediate winning continuations on the next O move are
c4 → c4 d4 e4 f4,
g4 → d4 e4 f4 g4,
f3 → c6 d5 e4 f3.
c4, g4, f3 are all reachable in one move, X can block at most one. Win forced on O’s next move. This is the textbook triple / double threat d4 e4 f4.

c4:
After O c4 row4 is c4 O d4 O e4 O. The only horizontal finisher is f4 → c4 d4 e4 f4. If X ≠ f4 O wins at once with f4. If X : f4 the column f is closed to row4 and f3 becomes playable, so O wins on the next move with c6 d5 e4 f3. Forced win in the same 2-ply horizon as f4.

g4:
After O g4 row4 is d4 O e4 O g4 O with f4 empty. The immediate horizontal finisher is f4 → d4 e4 f4 g4. If X ≠ f4 O wins at once with f4. If X : f4 the column f is closed to row4 and O wins on the next move with c6 d5 e4 f3. Forced win in the same 2-ply horizon.

Moves a4, b5, d3, e3 create no immediate forcing threat and are slower.

Notation confusion persists in the group: matrix row4 = 3rd from bottom in usual bottom-up Connect-4, and the diagonal win is often quoted as f3 bottom-up ≡ f4 matrix. Several colleagues therefore report the move as an immediate win in bottom-up notation, while in the printed matrix numbering the win is forced in two plies.

Disagreement:
* f4-only camp: claims f4 is the unique central triple threat c4/g4/f3 and c4/g4 are strictly slower / single-ended. Emphasises the open-ended double threat.
* f4 + c4 + g4 camp: notes c4 and g4 are symmetric row-4 three makers and also force a win in the minimum two-ply horizon, with the diagonal f3 as the back-up after X is forced to take f4.

Current belief: the minimum forced horizon is 2 O plies and it is attained by the row-4 forcing drops. Canonical realisation is the central triple threat f4. Up to left-right symmetry the same 2-ply forced win is obtained by c4 and by g4. Unresolved is whether g4 is considered distinct from the symmetric left-hand case by those who require a contiguous three on the move; the forcing argument above shows it still wins in two plies.

Row4 already has d4 O e4 O. The latent \ diagonal is c6 O d5 O e4 O with f3 becoming reachable once f4 is occupied.

* O:f4 → 4d O 4e O 4f O.  Row4 is an open three with both ends c4 and g4 playable and f3 becomes playable on the diagonal.  The three immediate winning continuations are
  c4 → c4 d4 e4 f4,
  g4 → d4 e4 f4 g4,
  f3 → c6 d5 e4 f3.
  X can take at most one of c4,g4,f3 on the intervening move, so O wins on the next O-move. This is the classic triple threat d4 e4 f4.

* O:c4 → 4c O 4d O 4e O.  The only immediate horizontal finisher on the rank is f4 → c4 d4 e4 f4.  If X≠f4 O wins at once with f4; if X:f4 the column f is closed to row4 and f3 becomes playable and O wins at once with c6 O d5 O e4 O f3 O.  Hence c4 forces a win in the minimum two-ply horizon.

* O:g4 → 4d O 4e O 4g O.  The immediate four d e f g is obtained with f4.  If X≠f4 O wins at once with f4 → d4 e4 f4 g4; if X:f4 the column f is closed to row4 and f3 becomes playable and O wins at once with c6 O d5 O e4 O f3 O.  X:f4 also makes the X diagonal 6d-5e-4f three, threatening 3g, but O wins with f3 before X can use it.  So g4 is also a two-ply forced win, the same line as c4 from the right.

a4,b5,d3,e3 create no immediate forcing threat and do not force a win in two plies. The minimum forced horizon is two O plies. Up to symmetry the row-4 forcing set is c4,f4,g4, with f4 the canonical central triple threat c4/g4/f3. Colleagues diverge on g4: several treat it as a non-contiguous three and therefore not a textbook open three, whereas the forcing analysis above shows it still forces f4 and the diagonal fallback f3 in the same two-ply horizon. The essentially unique strongest realisation remains the central f-drop, i.e. matrix f4, with the symmetric two-ply equivalents c4 and g4.

* O : c4
Row 4 becomes c4 O d4 O e4 O, a contiguous three is created on the move. The only immediate horizontal finisher on the rank is f4 → c4 d4 e4 f4. b4 is not a legal drop, the next free square in column b is b5, so the three is single-ended on the left. If X ≠ f4 O wins at once with f4. If X : f4 the column f is closed to row 4 and f3 becomes playable and O wins on the next move with c6 O d5 O e4 O f3 O. X can simply play X : f4 and the horizontal is stopped with no simultaneous second independent immediate winning square coming on line on the move.
